2 مرّح القِرْبَةَ , (inf. n. تَمْرِيحٌ, L,) (tropical:) He filled the water-skin with water in order that the punctures of the stitches might close up; i. q. سَرَّبَهَا. (S.) ―
-b2- Also, (tropical:) He rendered the water-skin sweet, when it was new, with إِذْخِر or with شِيح The rendering it sweet with loam or clay is termed تَشْرِيبٌ. (IAar.) ―
-b3- مرّح المَزَادَةَ (tropical:) He filled the مزادة with water, when it was new, in order that the punctures in it, made in sewing, might close up. (T, K.) ―
-b4- مرّح الجِلْدَ (assumed tropical:) He anointed the skin with oil. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
